# STM32H743 Nano FC + 4-in-1 ESC (Job #7): Design Model

I don't have the Job #7 design files, so every design value below is a stated assumption. Swap in your BOM values. Each model is written symbolically first and then evaluated numerically, so you can re-run it with your own numbers.

**Architectural note:** In a typical H743 + 4-in-1 stack, the H743 does not switch the bridges. The 48 kHz PWM is generated by the per-ESC MCU (AM32 or BLHeli_32 on an AT32F421, STM32G071, etc.). The H743's job is DShot600 command and decoding of bidirectional eRPM telemetry. The models below respect that split.

---

## 1. Baseline Assumptions

| Parameter | Symbol | Value | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Battery | V_bus | 25.2 V (6S full) | Worst case for switching loss |
| Burst phase current | I_ph | 80 A per ESC channel | Burst rating, not continuous |
| MOSFET | — | 40 V, 5×6 DFN class | e.g. a 0.8 mΩ-class part |
| R_DS(on) at 25 °C, V_GS = 10 V | R₂₅ | 0.80 mΩ | |
| R_DS(on) temperature coefficient | α | 0.0065 /K | ≈1.55× at 110 °C |
| Total gate charge | Q_g | 60 nC | |
| Miller charge | Q_gd | 10 nC | |
| Output charge at V_bus | Q_oss | 40 nC | |
| Body-diode reverse recovery | Q_rr | 50 nC | |
| Body-diode forward drop | V_f | 0.8 V | at 80 A |
| PWM frequency | f_sw | 48 kHz | |
| Dead time | t_dt | 100 ns | per edge |
| Gate drive voltage | V_drv | 10 V | FD6288Q-class driver |
| Gate resistor (external + internal + driver) | R_g,tot | ≈11 Ω | |
| Copper + connector resistance per phase path | R_cu | 0.30 mΩ | 2 oz copper, short pours |
| Ambient (inside frame) | T_a | 40 °C | |
| Maximum allowed junction temperature | T_j,max | 125 °C | Derated from 150/175 °C |

**Commutation scheme:** 6-step trapezoidal with synchronous rectification (the AM32/BLHeli_32 default). At any instant one high-side FET and one low-side FET carry I_ph. Each of the 6 FETs conducts for one third of the electrical cycle.

---

## 2. Conduction Loss Model (80 A Burst)

### 2.1 Temperature-dependent on-resistance

$$R_{DS}(T_j) = R_{25}\,[1 + \alpha (T_j - 25)]$$

At T_j = 110 °C: R = 0.80 × (1 + 0.0065 × 85) = **1.24 mΩ**.

### 2.2 Bridge conduction loss

With synchronous rectification, the PWM phase always has either its HS or LS FET conducting. Duty cycle therefore cancels, and two FETs are always in the current path:

$$P_{cond,bridge} = 2\, I_{ph}^2\, R_{DS}(T_j) \;-\; \underbrace{2\,I_{ph}^2 R_{DS}\,(2 t_{dt} f_{sw})}_{\text{dead-time correction, }<1\%}$$

$$P_{cond,bridge} = 2 \times 80^2 \times 1.24\times10^{-3} = \mathbf{15.9\ W}$$

**Per-FET loss (time-averaged):**

$$P_{cond,FET} = \tfrac{1}{3}\, I_{ph}^2 R_{DS} = 2.65\ \text{W}$$

The instantaneous loss during the FET's 120° conduction window is 7.9 W. At 30k RPM with a 14-pole motor, f_elec = 3.5 kHz, so the window lasts about 95 µs. That is much shorter than the die-to-case thermal time constant (around 1 to 5 ms), so the average value governs. At low RPM / high-torque stall, the 7.9 W instantaneous value governs and you must use Z_th(t) instead.

**Copper and shunt losses:**

$$P_{cu} = I_{ph}^2 R_{cu} = 6400 \times 0.3\,\text{m}\Omega = 1.9\ \
